validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, extensively documented infrastructure -- not a GEM-only entity. Independent of gem.wiki, found: Wikipedia, offshore-technology.com (two pages: /projects/sabah-sarawak/ and /marketdata/...), chemanalyst.com, Bernama (Malaysia's state news agency), and multiple Upstream Online headlines on its 2025 decommissioning. All corroborate the same physical pipeline (Sabah offshore fields -> Kimanis -> Bintulu MLNG). CLASSIFICATION: correctly a gas transmission trunk line (natural gas, GGIT), not a gathering/feeder line -- every source describes it as the trunk carrying Sabah gas to the Bintulu LNG complex. DUPLICATE: checked against the 5-pipeline Malaysia roster. Not the same project as P1067 'Trans Sabah Gas Pipeline' (cancelled) -- that is a separate, distinct proposed line; the Upstream headline 'Petronas gives up on ill-fated $1 billion gas pipeline' (cite_id cite_note-Upstream-7 on the wiki page) is actually about SSGP's OWN 2025 decommissioning/partial-shutdown announcement (cost and 'ill-fated' language match SSGP's well-documented leak/fire history and RM4.6bn/~US$1-1.5bn cost across chemanalyst and wascoenergy), not about Trans Sabah -- so no cross-contamination between the two rows. Not a segment double-count of P1065 (Peninsular Gas Utilization, a wholly separate west-coast/peninsular system) or P7105 (Malaysia-Singapore, a short spur far to the south). ATTRIBUTION: Owner = Petronas 100% confirmed independently by offshore-technology.com ('Owner/Operator: Petronas') and Bernama (state-owned asset, referenced as Petroliam Nasional Berhad) -- high tier, no other owner ever mentioned anywhere. Endpoints StartLocation=Kimanis/Sabah and EndLocation=Bintulu/Sarawak confirmed by offshore-technology.com and Wikipedia (both name Kimanis and Bintulu explicitly) -- high tier. SPEC: Length 512 km confirmed verbatim by chemanalyst.com AND offshore-technology.com/projects/sabah-sarawak/ (independent origins, both state '512-kilometre'/'512 kilometers'); Wikipedia and Bernama round to ~500 km, consistent, not a conflict -- high tier, matches GEM exactly. Diameter is genuinely BLANK on the sheet (verified against the live CSV: Diameter/DiameterUnits/Diameter [ref] all empty) -- chemanalyst.com and offshore-technology.com both independently give 36 inches; staged as a fill below. Capacity 7.70 bcm/y: only chemanalyst.com states an explicit number (750 MMcf/d) -- but that figure converts almost exactly to GEM's 7.70 bcm/y (750 MMcf/d x 365 d/y x 0.0283168 bcm/MMcf = ~7.75 bcm/y), so it corroborates the existing value even though it is a single explicit source (medium tier -- flagging so a future pass keeps looking for a second explicit number rather than treating this as closed). StartYear1=2014 confirmed independently by Bernama ('operational since early 2014') and chemanalyst.com -- high tier; offshore-technology.com's earlier order-year/2008-2011 construction-schedule figures describe the ORIGINAL (delayed) schedule, not a conflicting completion year. STATUS CAVEAT (why 'confirmed (caveat)' and not a plain confirm): as of 2025 reporting (chemanalyst.com, Bernama, Upstream headlines), Petronas has committed to decommissioning SSGP in stages, targeting completion before/by 2027, following a history of leaks/fires (2014, 2015, 2018, 2019, 2020, and a major September 2022 leak that triggered a force-majeure at MLNG); Petronas has stated 'parts of the SSGP will continue supplying gas to customers in Sabah' even as the through-line to Bintulu winds down. A third source (offshore-technology.com/marketdata page) additionally states the northern segment was 'permanently closed in August 2023,' but that specific claim could not be confirmed in the page's underlying fetched text via url_verifier (only the pipeline's name/length verified, not that sentence), so it is reported here as unverified color, not as a cited fact. Net: GEM's Status='operating' remains defensible today (partial service continues, decommissioning is not yet complete), but this is a live, actively-changing situation that a future sweep should re-check as 2027 approaches -- not a data error today.
